title: SMS Segments
summary: Shows how many billed SMS parts a text becomes and names the character (curly quote, emoji) that forced Unicode and raised the count.
description: SMS composer that splits text into the parts carriers bill (160/153 GSM-7, 70/67 UCS-2), names the curly quote or emoji that forced UCS-2 ("this ’ makes it 3 messages instead of 2"), fixes it in one tap, and reads the total back per recipient count.
catches: Characters outside GSM-7 that force UCS-2 (curly quotes, emoji, look-alikes)
Extension characters (€, [, ~) that use two septets
Part count and cost per recipient count
Never splits a 2-septet character or surrogate pair across parts
One-tap replace or remove of each culprit
limits: Assumes standard concatenation; some carriers or national shift tables differ
Cost uses the price you pass; carriers may bill differently
Replacing characters changes the text the recipient sees
a11y: Visible <label>; meter and warning linked via aria-describedby
Parts are buttons in a labelled group, each with an aria-label to select it
Warning renders in a polite live region; each fix has an aria-label
Highlight animation skipped under reduced motion

sources.label: ETSI TS 123 038 (3GPP TS 23.038) V17.0.0 – Alphabets and language-specific information

rules.note: Confirmed: 160 GSM 7-bit characters in 140 octets and the default alphabet extension table. The 153/67 per-part figures come from the concatenation header in 3GPP TS 23.040, not re-checked this round.

stops: One emoji doubled the SMS bill
